BiblicalUsage: Peace is the greeting kings send to the nations. Nebuchadnezzar writes to all people, nations, and languages: peace be multiplied unto you, and Darius writes the same. The king answers Rehum with peace, and the letter to Darius begins, all peace. The Aramaic word is prosperity, wholeness, the thing every king wishes for and cannot give.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the greeting gives the game away. Kings write peace to all the earth, and only God can multiply it, and I hold that true peace comes from Him alone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
